what: The brief's headline case — 250 label applications dropped at once — through the deployed batch UI on the unified-process build (commit 248b2bf: bands arrive with each row's verdict, the bold pass always runs and streams, bold_checking bucket). 250 rows assembled in the browser from the twelve bundled samples, each under its own filename, and fed through the real file-picker input as a CSV + 250 images.
pane_visible: YES — the browser pane was composited for the whole run, so the wall clock below is real elapsed time, not the throttled 'active processing time' the two earlier 250-row files carry. This is the measurement both of those files said was needed.

check_pass.note: 158.7s pane-visible vs 139.1s/146.5s pane-hidden on the pre-unification builds — consistent once renderer throttling is accounted for, and now carrying three upstream calls per row (transcription, bold judgment, band locator) instead of two.

bold_pass.ran: automatically, streaming during the check pass — no opt-in chip exists any more
bold_pass.note: The measurement finished BEFORE the check pass itself did (settled ~150s vs 158.7s), because bands now arrive with each row's verdict, so the expensive full-image band-repair OCR almost never fires. The pre-unification flow needed an additional opt-in pass after the run, estimated at ~17.5 minutes at its measured rate — that pass no longer exists as a separate phase.

settled_buckets.note: Matched means machine-cleared including a confident bold measurement. Need review is findings (field mismatches, warning failures) plus rows whose bold the measurement could not settle — each of those genuinely owes a human glance, and 59 of them are one-hover cards in the Confirm bold strip. No row sits in review because nobody has looked yet; the pre-unification build opened this same batch with all 250 rows in Needs review.

sample_batch_12_rows.note: Local dev run, pane visible: rows entered Checking bold at ~4s, resolved through it (never green mid-measurement), chip disappeared at settle. Replaces the uncited 'about 13 seconds' in submission.md.
